    Insurance has the unique closed class{0,1}; states2,3 eventually reach it. The higher-rate regime has unique closed class{2,3}; states0,1 eventually reach it. Each closed class has a self-loop and both income transitions, hence period1. Reducibility is therefore compatible with a unique globally attracting law; it is not evidence of multiple stationary distributions. All feasible alternatives were rechecked, and minimum positive gap bounds exceed0.0278 and0.0020 respectively.

    Insurance values are (-1.7769949740,-0.3296597913,-1.2266719737,0.1380640241); higher-rate values are (-4.2347061657,-1.4309947622,-3.4635695824,-0.9836825442). Initial welfare is the same fixed μ₀-weighted value in every regime. Relative to the baseline, insurance changes welfare by 1.5123143249, or 0.0756157162 after multiplying by1−β. The higher return changes it by -0.2171082600, normalized -0.0108554130. These are log-utility differences, not percentage GDP or an automatically compensated welfare gain for every foreign resident.

    Insurance smooths income directly and weakens precautionary saving; the eventual domestic net debt creates interest payments, so stationary domestic consumption199/200 is below one even though common-initial domestic welfare rises. In the higher-rate regime long-run assets rise and stationary domestic consumption exceeds one, yet common-initial welfare falls. Initial low-asset households face costlier contractual debt, and transition welfare is not summarized by the new stationary flow. The common initial mean asset position is zero, but its distribution and state-contingent consumption effects still matter.

    For any feasible state/action in any supplied regime, foreign consumption is at least W−R·max A+min A, whose smallest supplied value is2−(11/10)(1/4)−1/4=59/40>0. Thus the counterparty can fund every history and every cross-sectional mixture, not only the reported stationary choices. Summing C=y+τ+Ra−a′ and Cᴳ=W−Ra+a′ cancels each asset flow. The insurance table sums to3, as does the higher-rate table. The authority collects and pays equal aggregate transfers; foreign goods finance negative domestic saving. A household welfare gain is not a free world Pareto improvement: foreign consumption changes along transition and across stationary regimes, and their utility was not specified.

    No labor-supply response, search externality, sticky-price stabilization, default option or distortionary-tax cost was modeled. Those mechanisms from the rest of the volume cannot be inferred from this endowment experiment. Likewise, the rate stress is a change in the full contractual regime, including inherited date0 payoffs. An unexpected refinancing-only shock would require a separate inherited-rate state and newly dated budgets.

  6. 6. Three errors that must remain distinct

    After20 baseline value-iteration steps from zero the Bellman residual is 0.0452569154. Dividing by1−β gives a value-error bound 0.9051383077; the actual sup distance to the independently certified policy value is 0.9049852206, which lies below that bound. The final tighter residual is below10⁻¹⁰, hence the residual-based value bound is below2·10⁻⁹ before allowing numerical evaluation error. For a fully rational certificate use the explicit log and policy-system bounds in task2 rather than treating a floating residual as exact.

    On the refined grid the six-state policy is (0,1,0,2,1,2) and the invariant law is (1/3,1/12,1/12,1/12,1/12,1/3). Its graph is irreducible, includes a self-loop and is aperiodic. Direct multiplication verifies invariance. Mean assets remain zero and stationary domestic/foreign consumption remains1 and2, but finer smoothing changes conditional utility. Give the two new middle-asset states zero initial mass; common-initial welfare improves by 0.1816906558.

    Every old feasible history-dependent strategy is still feasible from an old initial state because its actions and inherited states belong to the refined grid; consumption and transition laws on those actions are unchanged. The supremum over the larger strategy set is therefore weakly higher at every old state. This proves the direction independently of a numerical table. The strict reported gain is certified only for this particular refinement. A small iteration residual bounds error relative to the finite-grid fixed point. A small distribution residual needs a mixing/invertibility bound before it bounds distribution distance. The difference between two grids is a sensitivity diagnostic, not an error bound relative to the continuous model: omitted interior actions, borrowing boundaries and policy discontinuities still matter. A credible continuous extension needs regularity, domain control, feasible interpolation and a justified operator discrepancy bound.

  7. 7. Execution is evidence with a limited scope

    The instructor package supplies a complete reproducible reference implementation and output; it does not certify the learner's independent implementation or oral defense. Run the files in a new five-file directory from a different working directory. Record the Python command, strict-JSON comparison and hashes. The normal and optimized checker gates separately reconstruct the economic quantities from primitives, compare all displayed values, and test the real CLI's protected writes. A small example of an invalid input is discount1 or a negative count; guards remain active under−O. A valid failure is setting foreign endowment to zero while retaining the private economy: the household problem can still be solved, but some foreign obligations cannot be funded, so the output reports a funding shortfall instead of certifying the project. Multiple closed classes or a periodic recurrent class likewise require explicit distribution diagnostics.

    Test each protected path as an output, then test a symbolic link and an existing hard link to it, in disposable copies. Verify every protected byte after each actual subprocess refusal; a successful call to a path-comparison helper is not a rejection test. Also test a normalized path containing a parent-directory segment. A manifest mismatch is a provenance failure, not automatically an economic error. Keep the distinction between author review, independent reconstruction and learner work.

    A defensible evidence memo would seek household panel observations of income transitions, asset choices, borrowing limits and consumption before and after an externally assigned insurance change. State the sampling unit, income measurement and attrition assumptions; quantify uncertainty in transition estimates rather than treating the synthetic sample size as real evidence. To estimate preferences or borrowing constraints, use additional moments and exclusion restrictions, check observationally similar parameter configurations and retain a separate validation sample. A possible reserved moment is the conditional saving response among initially low-income, low-asset households; do not fit that same response and advertise it as an independent test. A randomized or plausibly external policy assignment must still address take-up, labor incentives, spillovers and foreign funding effects. A common factor in observed interest rates is not itself causal identification.

    For the oral defense change one primitive, predict the affected feasibility or incentive inequality before rerunning, then explain any policy jump and altered recurrent class. Full credit requires a correct changed-model argument and truthful limits, not agreement with an insurance-policy conclusion. A successful numerical replication establishes the stated finite calculations; it does not establish real-world validity, unrestricted general equilibrium or research novelty.

Method sources and bounded transfer

The finite household problem is situated in the payoff-unit borrowing and stationary-distribution tradition of Huggett's revised1991 working paper, whose version and actual inspected scope were established in Chapter3. The conditional consumption-kernel context uses Sargent and Stachurski's finite-state asset-pricing lecture, inspected for Chapter7. Foreign-flow and price-taking distinctions connect to Uribe and Schmitt-Grohé's flow-collateral methods, inspected for Chapter10. Those sources motivate methods; none supplies these synthetic counts, policies, exact logarithm bounds, funded counterfactuals or project problems. Their continuous equilibrium, collateral or empirical results are not imported into this different finite endowment economy.

Oral transfer and teach-back

After written remediation, answer all five prompts aloud, allowing about5minutes each plus questioning. These suggested times are uncalibrated. Each carries4points; require17/20and at least3perdomain, with every critical error repaired. Explain assumptions without reading a stored answer, then respond to a changed premise supplied by the evaluator.

  1. Dynamic and distributional reasoning. A household policy holds its inherited wealth fixed forever, while income follows an iid two-state law with equal probabilities. Wealth has two possible levels0 and1. Explain every invariant joint distribution, why positive income probabilities do not guarantee unique wealth distribution, and what an Euler equality on a continuous choice domain says about this fixed discrete policy.
  2. State the policy equilibrium class. The deterministic two-jump-variable system is zₜ₊₁=Azₜ, A=diag(3/2,1/2), with no predetermined coordinate and bounded paths required. Characterize every bounded path. Explain how fiscal funding and labor-market efficiency remain separate questions even if an alternative monetary rule makes both eigenvalues exceed one.
  3. Explain marginal investment value. An owner has capital1 and current goods3. Choose I≥0 with current cost I+I²/2≤3. Terminal payoff is V(K)=6K−K²/2 with K=1+I, and discount1/2. The owner maximizes minus current cost plus discounted payoff. Find the global choice, both dates’ resource use, marginal q and discounted average asset value. Explain their difference.
  4. Change a currency numeraire correctly. Quote E as domestic currency per foreign unit, and let a foreign payoff be Z. Derive its foreign-currency price from a domestic SDF mD. State when mD(E₁/E₀) must equal a particular foreign household’s SDF, and explain why covered parity can hold with a nonzero currency premium.
  5. Defend a research claim. A calibrated model fits the mean and variance of a binary state and has a residual below10⁻¹⁰. A report calls its mechanism identified, causally validated and ready for a welfare recommendation. Give a precise four-part response and a feasible next empirical or computational task.
Complete solutions and additive scoring

  1. Each wealth class is closed; within it the invariant income law is(1/2,1/2). Therefore every joint law (t/2,t/2,(1−t)/2,(1−t)/2),0≤t≤1, is invariant in wealth-major order. Conversely stationarity forces each within-class income mass to split equally, so this is the entire family. Positive income transitions never move wealth and cannot establish joint irreducibility. A continuous Euler equality is not a necessary condition for a discrete-grid action; compare every feasible grid alternative or prove its Bellman inequality. An invariant distribution alone says nothing about that policy’s optimality.

    Rubric (4 points). Closed classes1; complete invariant family1; uniqueness failure1; discrete optimality/domain1. Study routes: v14-c01, v14-c03.

  2. Every path is((3/2)ᵗa,(1/2)ᵗb). Boundedness forcesa=0 but permits every finiteb, so the whole family is (0,(1/2)ᵗb). Two expanding eigenvalues would force both initial coefficients to zero in this homogeneous deterministic class; it is not a universal nonlinear/floor theorem. A fiscal intervention still needs a government present-value budget and defined transfers. Efficient search requires its matching, bargaining and planner conditions; determinacy of a monetary path cannot establish Hosios efficiency or a funded welfare improvement.

    Rubric (4 points). Full bounded family1; expanding comparison1; equilibrium-class restriction1; distinct fiscal/search conditions1. Study routes: v14-c04, v14-c05, v14-c06.

  3. The objective derivative is−1−I+(1/2)(5−I)=3/2−3I/2, with second derivative−3/2. Its unique unconstrained maximumI=1 satisfies the resource cap since cost3/2≤3, so it is also the unique constrained optimum. Current unused consumption is3/2; terminal payoffV(2)=10. Marginal q=(1/2)V′(2)=2 equals marginal installation cost1+I=2. Discounted average value is(1/2)V(2)/2=5/2. Thus (1,3/2,10,2,5/2) lists investment,current consumption,terminal payoff,q,average value. Concavity creates inframarginal rents; average value need not equal the marginal investment signal. The terminal claim belongs to the owner, with no extra unfinanced source of goods.

    Rubric (4 points). Global optimum/domain1; resources1; marginal q1; average distinction1. Study routes: v14-c07, v14-c08.

  4. Domestic cost isE[mD E₁ Z]; dividing by currentE₀ gives E[mD(E₁/E₀)Z], hence the transformed kernel. Equality to another kernel on every state requires a complete payoff span (positive state probabilities); equality of a single bond price gives only one expectation. Covered parity uses enforceable two-way financing/forward replication. Uncovered expected return additionally depends on Cov(mD,E₁/E₀); no-arbitrage replication does not force this covariance to zero. Binding dealer funding limits can also invalidate the covered replication assumptions, requiring their own portfolio constraints rather than an alleged free arbitrage.

    Rubric (4 points). Numeraire derivation1; spanning1; covariance distinction1; actual funding/replication domain1. Study routes: v14-c09, v14-c10.

  5. A binary state’s varianceμ(1−μ) is redundant with its mean, so counting the two does not establish identification; exhibit or exclude alternative parameters and add a discriminating moment. A residual needs the correct operator, norm and stability/error constant; it addresses numerical approximation. A causal claim needs an observation design, exogenous variation/exclusion and dependence-aware uncertainty; calibration is insufficient. Welfare needs defined preferences, distribution, funding, initial state and feasible policy. One next task is to hold the mean fixed while changing transition persistence, solve both policies with a true-operator certificate and predeclare a held-out lagged covariance test. If data access is absent, label this a synthetic method test, not a causal study.

    Rubric (4 points). Identification1; numerical certificate1; empirical design1; welfare and concrete next task1. Study routes: v14-c11, v14-c12.

Delayed retention with changed problems

Return after one to two weeks, then revisit weak domains after a month. Suggested allowance120minutes, without notes or code; extend it to preserve a full proof. Each task carries10points, total50. The instructional criterion is43/50and at least8perdomain. A memorized formula without a valid domain does not pass.

  1. Dynamic solution and distribution accuracy. For log utility, full depreciation and production2√k, discount4/5 and k₀=1, derive the optimal saving fraction, next capital and consumption. Explain the global supporting-tangent tail condition. Separately, a finite joint-distribution kernel has one-step minorization mass ε=1/4. A candidate invariant law has L1 residual1/25 and asset values in[0,2]. Derive bounds on distribution and mean assets.
  2. Reconstruct a search equilibrium. Consider continuous-time matching m=u^(1/2)v^(1/2), r=1/10,s=1/5, vacancy costκ=2/5, bargainingη=1/2, worker home flowb=1/5 and job outputy=61/125.   3. Price risk and repair debt overhang. States have probabilities(1/4,3/4), SDF(2,2/3), payoffX=(1,3). Find price, safe return, mean excess return and the Sharpe/Hansen–Jagannathan comparison. Separately, a firm has terminal asset50 and old debt65. An equity owner can prefund an investment cost10 that adds20 terminal assets. No other costs or discounting. Compare investment incentives and total surplus; find all renegotiated debt faces that weakly benefit both old creditor and equity relative to no investment, with investment undertaken.
  4. Close an international collateral experiment. Use the two-date tradable/nontradable model with log consumption of each good,β=ν=R=1, nontradable endowmentsone at both dates, y₀=2,y₁=5,inherited faceD=1. Foreigners have currentgoodsW=4 and invest unused resources atR=1. Compareκ=1/5 and1/10. Derive the unique borrowing equilibrium, both consumption/price pairs, net inflows and foreign investment, and reconcile both dates’ goods. Do not optimize as if an individual household controls the collateral price.
  5. Audit a network and a mechanism claim. Three institutions have nominal obligations(4,4,4), externalcash(1,1,1), and liability fractionsA12=1/2,A23=1/2,all otherinternal fractionszero. Claims share priority and there are no bankruptcy costs. Solve payments/equity/outside receipts, derive an L1residual certificate, and propagate an externalcash loss1/5 atnode1. Separately, two mechanism momentsg1=a+b,g2=2a+2b are(.1,.2); a newcontrastg3=a−b=.04 is proposed. State what it identifies and what empirical assumption the algebra does not supply.
Complete solutions and additive scoring

  1. The log Bellman coefficient isB=α/(1−αβ)=(1/2)/(3/5)=5/6. The saving shareβB/(1+βB)=2/5, so (2/5,4/5,6/5) lists share,next capital,consumption. Concavity and the Euler equality telescope a finite-horizon utility-gain bound; nonnegative alternative capital leaves at mostβᵀs/(1−s)=(4/5)ᵀ(2/3), tending tozero. Feasible alternative capital is bounded above, so positive utility parts are summable and even negative-infinite alternatives are covered. Mere Bellman substitution would not supply this comparison. Minorization contracts signed probability differences in L1 by1−ε=3/4. The residual triangle bound is(1/25)/(1/4)=4/25. Since probability differences sum tozero, center assets at1: mean error≤1·L1error=4/25. This is not the generally looser max-absolute-assets bound2·L1.   2. Withf=√θ,q=1/√θ, stationarity and values imply the free-entry scalarκ[(r+s)√θ+ηθ]=(1−η)(y−b). The left side is strictly increasing forθ>0, startszero and diverges, while the right ispositive; hence one active root. Writingx=√θ yields(2/5)[(3/10)x+x²/2]=18/125, solved byx=3/5.   3. E[m]=1 and priceE[mX]=1/2+3/2=2, hence safe return1 and risky returns(1/2,3/2). Mean gross return5/4 gives excess1/4. SDF variance1/3 and risky-return variance3/16 give Sharpe(1/4)/(√3/4)=1/√3, exactlyσ(m)/E[m]; the centered return is negatively proportional to centeredm. (1/3,3/16,1/4) records the variances and premium. Equality is meaningful because both variances are positive. Without investment equity receiveszero and creditors50. Maxinternal row sum1/2 contracts the transpose inL1, so an approximate payment residual1/100 bounds error by 1/50. The cashloss produces paymentlosses (1/5,1/10,1/20); grossloss7/20 exceeds cashloss, while outside loss1/10+1/20+1/20=1/5. Internal claims cancel; no extra resources vanished. Remediation and reassessment

Keep an error ledger with the exact prompt, mistaken inference, corrected derivation, violated assumption and a new transfer problem. Classify an error by its cause rather than by the chapter title: a sign mistake in a foreign balance sheet differs from failing to name the currency numeraire; a grid residual differs from the original Bellman residual.

  • Budget, terminal or ownership error: redraw every dated real resource and claim flow, label counterparties, and sum the accounts before optimizing. Return to chapters1,2,6,8,10.
  • Optimization or equilibrium error: list every feasible action and boundary, distinguish necessary conditions from a global comparison, and check every market. Return to chapters1–5and8–10.
  • Distribution error: build the joint transition, find closed classes and verify mass, invariance and initial conditions. Return to chapter3and the quantitative project.
  • Pricing or leverage error: state numeraire, payoff date, investor opportunity set and funding. Verify the same payoff under both strategies before alleging arbitrage. Return to chapters7–10.
  • Evidence error: write the observation law and moment map, separate numerical/parameter/model uncertainty, and disclose adaptation of held-out data. Return to chapters11–12and Volume12.

Redo the failed part from blank paper, explain it aloud, then solve a genuinely changed problem before taking the alternate written form. A correct copied solution is a study aid, not evidence of mastery. Record unresolved conceptual errors for a human instructor rather than compensating for them with extra calculation points.

Concept and outcome index

  1. Chapter1: Prove dynamic optimality with a correct terminal comparison and certify its numerical solution.
  2. Chapter2: Connect the stochastic growth allocation to private incentives and distinguish exact from local dynamics.
  3. Chapter3: Track joint heterogeneity, constrained saving and aggregate assets/goods, including finite-grid limitations.
  4. Chapter4: Derive labor values, entry and unemployment dynamics; assess efficiency under stated matching assumptions.
  5. Chapter5: Derive nominal rigidity and a properly qualified bounded equilibrium under monetary rules.
  6. Chapter6: Close fiscal funding, distinguish policy determinacy and welfare, and solve finite sovereign default.
  7. Chapter7: Price consumption risk and explain the limits of habit/recursive-preference and empirical puzzle claims.
  8. Chapter8: Solve investment/agency/collateral constraints and account for debt overhang and financial propagation.
  9. Chapter9: Check run incentives, off-path liquidity resources, leverage feedback and constrained risk-bearing.
  10. Chapter10: Solve cross-border risk sharing, currency conversion, sudden stops and global state pricing.
  11. Chapter11: Separate true-model numerical error from parameter identification, sampling and held-out performance.
  12. Chapter12: Design a tractable, dated and falsifiable research contrast with honest evidence and access limits.

The examinations assess these outcomes through specified small models; their coverage maps identify which subparts do so. A finite solved example is not evidence that the learner can solve every model in the literature. The project adds reproducible implementation, while later research work requires original questions, new evidence and expert judgment.

Volume synthesis

Dynamic optimization, equilibrium accounting and empirical identification are complementary. A household policy may be optimal but fail aggregate clearing; a price system may clear a finite market yet say little about a causal policy effect; a calibrated model may reproduce targets while leaving its central mechanism unidentified. Distributional states, nominal and financial constraints, and international claims enrich the mechanisms but do not remove these logical distinctions.

Carry forward three habits: derive incentives over the actual feasible set and every relevant history; consolidate counterparties before reporting aggregate resources or welfare; and state what observable contrast could reject the interpretation. The graduate qualifying sequence combines these macro-finance skills with econometrics and microeconomic theory. Economic fields and institutions then supplies substantive settings; the research, teaching and leadership portfolios require work and evaluation beyond reading a textbook.

Sources and scope of review

All tasks, inputs and grading designs here are original. The underlying methods are taught and proved in the linked accepted chapters. Stable primary method routes are Sargent and Stachurski’s discrete dynamic programming lecture, Galí’s basic New Keynesian notes, and Uribe and Schmitt-Grohé’s financial-frictions slides. Their prior inspection scopes are retained in the source record; this support package claims no new full-paper or image inspection. No source examination has been copied. Machine-assisted review of these materials does not substitute for independent human evaluation of a learner’s research or professional judgment.
